In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of soman on the binding of muscarinic antagonist [3H]quinuclidinylbenzilate([3H]QNb) to its receptor (M-AChR) in vivo.
the interaction between soman and M-AChRs in vivo, which is a new finding in soman research.
the interaction of soman with M-AChR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the binding of soman to M-AChR was not the only mechanism of soman-induced inhibition of M-AChR.
soman inhibits the M-AChR function by a direct action on the receptors, which is independent of the inhibition of ChE.
soman inhibited the specific binding of M-AChR with [3H]-QNB in rat whole brain homogenates in vivo in a competitive manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dual action of soman on M-AChR and ChE may be a common phenomenon in the central and peripheral nervous systems.
soman could inhibit [3H]NMS or [3H] QNB binding in vitro or in vivo, the inhibition was competitive and took place before complete ChE inhibition.
soman inhibited the M-AChR function by two ways: 1, direct interaction with the receptor; 2, inhibition of ACh release by inhibition of ChE.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inhibition of M-AChR by soman in vivo is a competitive one and the inhibition of ChE by soman is not the sole reason for its action on M-AChR.
soman can be used as a tool to study the function of muscarinic receptors.
